video_title: POSTGAME SOUND: ORLANDO MAGIC VS. GOLDEN STATE WARRIORS | COACH SWEENEY, CAIN & WAGNER

quotes.speaker: Coach Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Mosley on Orlando's offensive rebounding and turnover management
quotes.excerpt: I thought just in general, we did a great job on the offensive boards.
quotes.quote: They started off getting to the free throw line and a couple plays early. Bassi got a couple free throws early, and then they did a good job of executing down the stretch. I thought we did a good job, got some good looks, some guys made some big-time plays. I thought just in general, we did a great job on the offensive boards. It was a point of emphasis for us. We had a number of guys get three-plus. Got to keep that up. I thought we did a great job of taking care of the basketball throughout the night. Point of emphasis for us was taking care of it and got those turnovers way down. We got to keep doing that and then we just got to build on it.
quotes.social_post: Coach Mosley credits the Magic for a strong effort on the offensive boards and better ball security against the Warriors.

structured.context: Coach Jamahl Mosley discusses the team's performance regarding offensive rebounding and turnover management following the game against the Golden State Warriors.

quotes.speaker: Coach Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Mosley on the challenge of defending Stephen Curry
quotes.excerpt: If you do a good job early getting them under control, he's still going to stick with it.
quotes.quote: It's tough. All-time great player and did a great job throughout the course of the game. The thing with him is he's never done. Even if you do a good job early getting them under control, he's still going to stick with it. Before the end of the half, he got a couple baskets, got going there, and down the stretch made some tough ones. You can't let up with him, and that's why he's one of the greatest of all time.
quotes.social_post: Coach Mosley on defending Stephen Curry: You can never let up because he is never done. That is why he is one of the greatest of all time.

structured.context: Coach Jamahl Mosley reflects on the difficulty of defending Stephen Curry throughout the game.

quotes.speaker: Coach Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Mosley on Orlando's third quarter aggressiveness and paint protection
quotes.excerpt: I really like the aggressiveness that we had attacking the boards on both ends.
quotes.quote: I really like the aggressiveness that we had attacking the boards on both ends. I thought we did a great job of taking care of the basketball. The two things I wanted to see us do a little bit better job of was contesting their shots, which I thought we did a very nice job of, and then really trying to touch that paint, which I thought we did a better job of and did a good job in the third quarter. A number of guys really attacking in that third quarter. I think we had 37 for the quarter, tightened up on both ends, did a good job.
quotes.social_post: Coach Mosley liked the aggressiveness in the third quarter and the team's ability to attack the paint.

structured.context: Coach Jamahl Mosley analyzes the team's third-quarter aggressiveness and defensive paint protection.

quotes.speaker: Coach Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Mosley on Wendell Carter Jr.'s rebounding performance
quotes.excerpt: A number of guys did a great job getting on the boards, Wendell had six.
quotes.quote: A number of guys did a great job getting on the boards, Wendell had six. We saw a number of guys crashing from the perimeter the way we want to. We got to keep that up, and the more opportunities, the more bites at the apple you get, the better chances you are to get something done. So I thought we did a really good job of that throughout the course of the game, especially in that third quarter. I thought we really did a great job of it.
quotes.social_post: Coach Mosley highlights Wendell Carter Jr. and the team's commitment to crashing the glass from the perimeter.

structured.context: Coach Jamahl Mosley praises Wendell Carter Jr. for his rebounding performance during the game.

quotes.speaker: Coach Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Mosley on Jamal Cain's energy and rebounding
quotes.excerpt: I thought he did a great job giving great energy. Obviously the points reflect him scoring.
quotes.quote: I thought he did a great job giving great energy. Obviously the points reflect him scoring, but I thought he did a great job really attacking the offensive boards and the defensive boards for that matter. I think he had three or more, four offensive rebounds and then eight defensive rebounds. That's big for us, you know, when he's out there being aggressive to try to get that done and then giving great effort on both ends.
quotes.social_post: Coach Mosley praises Jamal Cain for his energy and rebounding effort against Golden State.

structured.context: Coach Jamahl Mosley highlights the energy and rebounding effort provided by Jamal Cain.

quotes.speaker: Jamal Cain
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamal Cain on Stephen Curry's impact in crunch time
quotes.excerpt: They had one of the best players in the world on their team, he capitalized.
quotes.quote: They had one of the best players in the world on their team, he capitalized in the crunch time. But I'm happy with how we competed though. I think we competed the whole game and we gave ourselves a chance to win, but they got 30 on the other side, so.
quotes.social_post: Jamal Cain on the loss to the Warriors: They have one of the best players in the world and he capitalized in crunch time.

structured.context: Jamal Cain discusses the impact of Stephen Curry's performance during the crunch time of the game.

quotes.speaker: Jamal Cain
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamal Cain on providing a spark off the bench
quotes.excerpt: I just wanted to bring an edge and a spark off the bench.
quotes.quote: It's extremely important because we have three of our most important guys down right now, so we know guys got to step up. And I just wanted to bring an edge and a spark off the bench, you know, trying to help us get some life.
quotes.social_post: Jamal Cain says he is focused on bringing an edge and a spark off the bench while the Magic deal with key injuries.

structured.context: Jamal Cain explains his role in providing a spark off the bench while the team deals with multiple player injuries.

quotes.speaker: Jamal Cain
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamal Cain on his growth in confidence since training camp
quotes.excerpt: I would say confidence for sure. I think I'm way more confident, more level with this team.
quotes.quote: I would say confidence for sure. I think I'm way more confident, more level with this team because you know I'd have been with them last year in crunch time games, so I think the confidence is the biggest growth for me.
quotes.social_post: Jamal Cain credits his growth this season to increased confidence and familiarity with the team.

structured.context: Jamal Cain reflects on his personal growth and increased confidence since training camp.

quotes.speaker: Franz Wagner
quotes.summary_phrase: Franz Wagner on the team's inability to get defensive stops
quotes.excerpt: I don't think we were able to get as many stops as we needed obviously.
quotes.quote: I don't think we were able to get as many stops as we needed obviously. It's fair to say they got one of the best players in the league on the team and I think I think we weren't able in those critical moments to get two stops and no couple scores in a row and.
quotes.social_post: Franz Wagner admits the Magic struggled to get the necessary defensive stops in critical moments against Stephen Curry.

structured.context: Franz Wagner discusses the team's failure to secure necessary defensive stops against Stephen Curry in critical moments.

quotes.speaker: Franz Wagner
quotes.summary_phrase: Franz Wagner on the team's offensive rebounding improvement
quotes.excerpt: Really important for us going forward too, so big improvement there.
quotes.quote: Really important for us going forward too, so big improvement there and no got to find a way to keep doing that.
quotes.social_post: Franz Wagner emphasizes that the team's improvement on the offensive glass is a key focus moving forward.

structured.context: Franz Wagner comments on the team's improvement in offensive rebounding.

quotes.speaker: Franz Wagner
quotes.summary_phrase: Franz Wagner on his playmaking and turnover issues
quotes.excerpt: I had a bunch of turnovers tonight again, so obviously made a couple bad reads there.
quotes.quote: I think it's been good at times, you know what I mean? I had a bunch of turnovers tonight again, so obviously made a couple bad reads there and yeah, I think like I said though, I think it's been it's been good at times and I got to find a way to be more consistent and take care of the ball a little better.
quotes.social_post: Franz Wagner on his recent turnover struggles: I made a couple bad reads and I have to find a way to be more consistent and take care of the ball.

structured.context: Franz Wagner addresses his recent playmaking performance and the need to reduce turnovers.

quotes.speaker: Franz Wagner
quotes.summary_phrase: Franz Wagner on Jamal Cain's aggressive performance
quotes.excerpt: I thought Jamal played great, like I said, really aggressive and need him to continue to do that.
quotes.quote: I thought Jamal played great, like I said, really aggressive and need him to continue to do that.
quotes.social_post: Franz Wagner praises Jamal Cain for his aggressive play and hopes to see him keep that energy up.

structured.context: Franz Wagner praises the aggressive play of his teammate Jamal Cain.
